issues.spec_citation: FHIR R4 base64Binary; sql-on-fhir-v2 library-profiles.fsh content.data 1..1
issues.evidence: content[].data rejects URL-safe alphabet (-/_), embedded whitespace/newlines, missing/extra padding, and empty string with typed SQLQueryParseError. Consistent with SKEPTIC launch's deliberate strict-base64 fix; FHIR JSON strings carry the standard alphabet only.

Library.type.coding containing the expected code pinned to a foreign code system raises SQLQueryParseError even when a later coding carries the correct LibraryTypesCodes system. Strictest-coding-first is consistent with the HISTORIAN type-coding-system fix (a same-code/different-system coding is a different concept).
issues.root_cause: Intentional strict rejection of foreign-system codings.

issues.spec_citation: library-profiles.fsh contentType extensible binding to AllSQLContentTypeCodes; sql-must-be-sql-expressions invariant (startsWith 'application/sql')
issues.evidence: contentType 'application/sql;charset=utf-8' passes parse+validate (invariant only requires the application/sql prefix) but the runner's select_best_content raises UnsupportedDialectError because only exact 'application/sql' and 'application/sql;dialect=duckdb' are supported. Spec permits unenumerated codes; treating charset params as generic SQL at execution time would be a compatible enhancement.
issues.resolution: Deferred: parse-side behavior is spec-correct; execution-side charset tolerance is an optional enhancement outside this chunk's invariants.
